title: S16 The «locale PEN» money contract misreads Peru's own format.
description:
[O] The «locale PEN» money contract misreads Peru's own format. Rule (2) treats «coma y punto» as dot = thousands, comma = decimal. Peru's actual convention (CLDR `es-PE`; `Intl.NumberFormat('es-PE',{currency:'PEN'})` → «S/ 1,250.50») is the reverse. Running `norm_money` from theory[6] on «S/ 1,250.50» returns `1.2505` and on «S/ 1,250» returns `1.25` (verified), a 1000× error on the receipts Lucía sees every day in Lima. The section calls this the documented PEN locale and teaches it as the guard against KPI distortion.

title: S20 The You Do's central gate checks nothing.
description:
[O] The You Do's central gate checks nothing. In the starter, `portada` is read back from `Salida!B1`, the cell `materialize_salida` just filled with `det_sum`, and `n_xlsx` is read back from the `n_rows` it just wrote. `reconcile(det_sum, portada, …)` therefore compares a number with itself. It catches only "forgot to write the cell", never a wrong sum. The same goes for idempotency: `"idempotent": dig_a == dig_b` digests the same `rows` list reversed, and `dig_rows` sorts first, so the result is True by construction. The process is never run twice. Theory promises the opposite: «aquí se comprueba corriendo el proceso dos veces y comparando». The `backup` copies the fresh `out` straight after copying the master, so it is not a backup of a previous result. Lucía will see `reconcile_ok True` and `idempotent True` whether her code is right or not.

Dónde (campo del contenido): `youDo.starterCode` (steps 3–5), `theory[0].paragraphs[3]`
actual: Evidencia: «portada = sal["B1"].value if sal["B1"].value is not None else -1.0» / «dig_b = dig_rows(list(reversed(rows)))  # mismo multiconjunto, otro orden»
improvement: `src/lib/course/sections/s20-rag.ts`: reconcile against an independent source, either a `pd.read_csv` of the synthetic input or a `portada` cell the template already holds, and include one deliberately wrong fixture that must print `reconcile_ok False`. Prove idempotency by running `run_factory(input)` twice and comparing `dig_rows` of the two `Salida` sheets read back from disk. Back up the *previous* `results.xlsx` before overwriting it. [O] The You Do starter already "passes" everything without any work, and it models the human approval as automatic. `advance("approve")` appends `{"action": "approve", "actor": "r1"}` by itself, `hitl` starts at all zeros, and `package_e2e()` hard-codes `"n2_regression": "pass"`, `cost_tokens 1200` and `value_minutes_saved_est 45`. Running the untouched starter prints seven `success`, `can_draft_after True` and `package pass 45`. iDo.steps[7] and theory[9] do the same thing with literals such as `print("audit", …, "fraud_labels", 0, "n2_regression", "pass")`, while the preamble asks her to predict «por qué `n2_regression` es `pass` (re-run real)».

Dónde (campo del contenido): `youDo.starterCode` (`advance`, `package_e2e`), `iDo.steps[7].code`, `theory[9].code`
actual: Evidencia: «"n2_regression": "pass",  # re-run real: CP-N2-A/B/C + privacy + CF-2»
improvement: `s26-integrator-phase1.ts`: make `approve` require an explicit `decide(action, actor, reason)` call from outside `run_all`. Compute `n2_regression` from an actual `subprocess.run` of the three capstone test files, and start `hitl` with pending items. (This is a tautological check: the section's own rule «no "planned"» is broken by its scaffold, and the "human" in HITL is the code.)
label: O

title: S26 The DAG theory claims cycle detection that no code performs.
description:
[O] The DAG theory claims cycle detection that no code performs. Theory says «si hay ciclo, el pipeline **no arranca**», but `topo()` (Kahn) silently returns a shorter list on a cycle. iDo.steps[0]'s `order_from_edges` only follows a linear chain and silently drops any branch. No exercise adds a cycle test, so Lucía leaves believing her topo sort protects her.
